identity.title: MMIE: Massive Multimodal Interleaved Comprehension Benchmark for Large Vision-Language Models

problem.claim: Evaluate interleaved multimodal comprehension and generation in large vision-language models.

gap.claim: Existing evaluation is limited in scale, scope, and depth, and metrics may be costly, biased, and insufficiently reliable for practical use.

contributions.claim: Introduces MMIE, a knowledge-intensive benchmark with 20K curated queries across 3 categories, 12 fields, and 102 subfields.
Supports interleaved inputs and outputs with both multiple-choice and open-ended formats.
Proposes an automated metric based on a scoring model fine-tuned on human annotations and systematic criteria, aimed at reducing bias and improving accuracy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a large-scale, broad-coverage interleaved LVLM benchmark together with a human-annotated-data-based automated evaluation metric.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report that experiments found the benchmark and metrics effective for comprehensive evaluation of interleaved LVLMs.
Authors report evaluating eight LVLMs; even the best showed substantial room for improvement, and most achieved only moderate results.

narrative_sequence.summary: Interleaved multimodal understanding and generation are framed as an important multimodal-learning capability.
The abstract identifies insufficient evaluation, citing limitations in benchmark scale, scope, depth, and metric reliability.
MMIE is introduced with broad knowledge coverage, interleaved input/output support, and mixed question formats.
A human-annotation-informed automated metric is proposed, followed by experiments on eight LVLMs showing moderate performance and remaining improvement room.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark combines broad domain coverage, interleaved inputs and outputs, and multiple question formats.

lessons.interpretation: A capability claim becomes more informative when the evaluation dimensions are made explicit rather than represented by one task format.
lessons.application: Define an evaluation matrix covering domains, modality order, output modality, and response format before reporting aggregate results.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when the target deployment has a narrowly defined domain or interaction format.

source_observation.claim: The proposed metric uses human-annotated data and systematic criteria to address bias and accuracy concerns.

lessons.interpretation: Automated evaluation can be framed around an explicit human-grounded scoring protocol.
lessons.application: Document annotation criteria and use them to fine-tune or calibrate an automated judge for open-ended multimodal outputs.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when annotation coverage is too sparse or the scoring criteria cannot capture essential task-specific qualities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark splits, dataset sources, contamination controls, or per-category results.
The reported metric effectiveness lacks quantitative comparisons, uncertainty estimates, and detailed validation conditions.
The abstract does not establish priority or independently verify the authors' novelty, experimental claims, or metric reliability.
